summary: The associative product-free Lambek calculus L as a sequent calculus with the non-empty-antecedent condition; cut admissibility and Gentzen's Hauptsatz by Lambek's degree/height induction; the subformula property; a shallow Curry-Howard reading of derivations as Coq functions; a Montague fragment where the derivations of 'every/some man walks' compute the quantified meanings by conversion.

sources.citation: Lambek, J. (1958). The mathematics of sentence structure. Amer. Math. Monthly 65(3):154-170.
Moot, R. & Retoré, C. (2012). The Logic of Categorial Grammars. LNCS 6850. Ch. 2-3.
Moortgat, M. (1997). Categorial type logics. Handbook of Logic and Language, ch. 2.

definitions_mapped.note: non-empty antecedent as a Prop side condition on the right rules; derivations in Type

definitions_mapped.source: M&R §3.3 steps 2-3; Moortgat Def. 3.2 term assignment
definitions_mapped.note: terms are Coq functions (shallow), not a syntactic λ-calculus

definitions_mapped.source: M&R Ex. 3.5, Ex. 3.2; Lambek Table I

evidence: Rules are the six of M&R Fig. 2.2 minus the product rules, with Lambek's side condition (Lambek.v Part 2).
Cut elimination follows Lambek's own induction on degree and length; the case table is documented at cut_adm_aux.
The fragment derivations denote exactly the Montague meanings of M&R Ex. 3.5/3.2 by conversion (Part 6).
Print Assumptions: all ten main theorems closed under the global context.
simplifications: λ-terms read shallowly as Coq functions, so β-conversion is definitional
omissions: decidability by fuel-bounded proof search (Lambek §8 decision procedure) not formalized
semantic invariance of cut elimination (denote (cut_elim d) = denote d) not proved (cut_adm opaque)
syntactic term calculus with 'cut elimination preserves the term up to β'
additions: Type-valued list-splitting lemmas for Lambek's seven-case analysis

determination_rationale: The calculus, its cut elimination and subformula property, and the Curry-Howard semantics go through exactly as in the sources with no extra assumptions; the only encoding cost is representational (holes as list concatenations, derivations in Type).

artifact_classes.description: derivations in Type rather than a Prop relation, so that cut elimination and denotation compute
sequent holes as list concatenations; position analysis via Type-valued splitting lemmas and transports
Prop-valued stdlib list lemmas cannot build derivations; Type-valued twins written
shallow terms make β-conversion invisible; the term-level cut-elimination theorem is not statable

notes: Built by hand in-session after the agent pipeline was stopped; 904 lines. Remaining design items (decidability, syntactic terms, models) recorded in the file header under 'Not formalized'.
